title: Joshua Commissioned
summary: After Moses' death the LORD tells Joshua to cross the Jordan and promises that no one will stand against him if he is strong, keeps the law, and meditates on it day and night. Joshua orders the officers to prepare provisions for crossing in three days. He reminds Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh of their promise to cross armed with their brothers, and they answer that they will obey him as they obeyed Moses.

title: Rahab and the Spies
summary: Joshua sends two spies from Shittim to Jericho, where they lodge in the house of Rahab, a prostitute. When the king's men come, she hides them under stalks of flax on the roof and sends the searchers away. She says the people of the land fear Israel's God and asks that her family be spared. The spies promise, tell her to bind a scarlet cord in her window and keep her family in the house, and report to Joshua.

title: Crossing the Jordan
summary: At Joshua's command the people follow the ark carried by the priests, keeping about 2,000 cubits back. When the priests' feet touch the Jordan at flood stage, the water upstream stands in a heap and Israel crosses on dry ground. Twelve men, one from each tribe, take stones from the riverbed to set up at Gilgal as a memorial for children to ask about, and Joshua sets up twelve stones in the river as well. The priests come up and the waters return.

title: Circumcision and Passover at Gilgal
summary: After the crossing, the Canaanite kings lose heart. The LORD tells Joshua to circumcise the men born in the wilderness, and the place is called Gilgal. Israel keeps the Passover on the fourteenth day, eats the produce of the land, and the manna stops. Near Jericho Joshua meets a man with a drawn sword, the commander of the LORD's army, who tells him to remove his sandals because the ground is holy.

title: The Fall of Jericho
summary: Following the LORD's instructions, Israel marches around Jericho once a day for six days with seven priests blowing trumpets before the ark, and seven times on the seventh day. At Joshua's command the people shout, the wall falls flat, and Israel takes the city, devoting everything to destruction except silver, gold, bronze and iron for the LORD's treasury. Rahab and her household are brought out and spared, and Joshua curses anyone who rebuilds Jericho.

title: Achan's Sin and Ai
summary: Achan takes some of the devoted goods from Jericho, and the LORD's anger burns against Israel. Israel is defeated at Ai, and Joshua tears his clothes and prays. Lots identify Achan, who confesses to taking a robe, silver and a wedge of gold; he and his family are stoned in the valley of Achor. Israel then takes Ai by ambush, and Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal, writes the law on stones, and reads the blessings and curses to all Israel.

title: The Gibeonite Deception
summary: When the kings of Canaan unite to fight Joshua, the people of Gibeon send ambassadors in worn clothes and moldy bread, claiming to come from a far country. Israel's leaders make a treaty with them without asking the LORD. Three days later they learn that the Gibeonites live nearby, but the oath holds, and the Gibeonites are made woodcutters and water carriers for the congregation and the altar.

title: The Sun Stands Still
summary: Five Amorite kings attack Gibeon, and Joshua marches all night from Gilgal to defend it. The LORD throws the enemy into confusion and sends great hailstones that kill more than Israel's swords. Joshua asks the sun to stand still over Gibeon and the moon over Ajalon until the battle is won, and the text says there was no day like it. The five kings are caught in a cave at Makkedah, killed and hung, and Joshua conquers cities of the south.

title: Northern Campaign and the Land Taken
summary: Jabin, king of Hazor, gathers a northern coalition with horses and chariots, but the LORD tells Joshua not to fear. Israel routs them at the waters of Merom, hamstrings the horses, burns the chariots, and burns Hazor. Joshua takes the hill country and the south, leaving only the Anakim in the Philistine cities. Chapter 12 lists the thirty-one kings defeated west of the Jordan, along with the two kings Moses defeated to the east.

title: Dividing the Land
summary: Joshua is old, and the LORD tells him much land remains to be taken. He distributes the land by lot to the nine and a half tribes, after Moses has already given the east bank to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh. Caleb claims Hebron at eighty-five and drives out the Anakim, and Joshua receives Timnath-serah. Six cities of refuge are named, and the Levites receive forty-eight cities, with the closing note that not one promise failed.

title: The Altar by the Jordan
summary: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh return east of the Jordan and build a large altar at the river's edge. The rest of Israel gathers at Shiloh to go to war, but first sends Phinehas and ten chiefs to accuse them of rebellion, recalling Peor and Achan. The eastern tribes answer that the altar is a witness that they too belong to the LORD, not a place for sacrifice. Phinehas is satisfied, and the altar is named Ed, a witness.

title: Joshua's Farewell and Covenant at Shechem
summary: Old and well along in years, Joshua gathers Israel's leaders and warns them to keep the law, not to mix with the nations left in the land, and not to serve their gods. At Shechem he recounts Israel's history from Terah to the conquest and tells the people to choose whom they will serve, declaring, 'as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.' The people agree, and Joshua makes a covenant and sets up a stone. He dies at 110, and Joseph's bones are buried at Shechem.
